label: William Neil McCasland
narrative: McCasland is the point where this board and The Vanishing become the same board. A retired Air Force major general who commanded the Air Force Research Laboratory at Wright-Patterson Air Force Base, he vanished from his Albuquerque home in February 2026, leaving behind his phone, prescription glasses, hiking boots, wallet and a .38-calibre revolver. Rep. Eric Burlison revealed on 21 April 2026 that his staff had been trying to reach McCasland in connection with a separate congressional investigation before he disappeared, and that his disappearance is what triggered the House Oversight probe that Chairman Comer and Burlison opened into eleven people in nuclear or rocket-adjacent work who have died or vanished since 2022. Burlison's stated reasoning is the reasoning of an investigator: 'How many people walk out their front door without their phone, their wallet, their keys, or anything?' The committees demanded briefings from the FBI, the Department of War, NASA and the Department of Energy by 27 April 2026. McCasland's institutional position is the reason his name carries the nickname the press has given him: AFRL at Wright-Patterson is the single installation most persistently named in the legacy recovery literature, and he commanded it.
